p: A few practical tips for a night in the Cavern Quarter. Bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues commonly check. If you're a stag or hen group, book well ahead, as weekends in this part of town are extremely popular. More than six of you? Two lanes will keep everyone involved and stop the night grinding to a halt between turns.

Liverpool Lime Street station is a short walk away, and Moorfields and Liverpool Central stations are even closer, so getting here by train is simple. The area gets very lively late at night, so it's worth having a plan for getting home, whether that's a train, a taxi rank or a pre-booked cab.

If you've got time during the day, there's loads of history close by. St George's Hall, near Lime Street, is a magnificent neoclassical building that hosts events and tours. The Walker Art Gallery and World Museum sit right next to it. And the Williamson Tunnels, a strange network of underground passages built in the 19th century by an eccentric local businessman, are a fascinating and unusual visit.

With a bit more time, a trip on the Mersey Ferry gives you the classic view of the waterfront from the water, and a short train ride north takes you to Crosby Beach, where Antony Gormley's iron figures stand gazing out to sea. A great mix of sights before a night of bowling and music.
